data.claim: api.ci.run only returns an Outcome; only gate run records
data.falsifier: ci run from an item records gate ci
data.mechanism: no call to gates.record in the ci path
data.probe_output: before fix: KeyError recorded / no ci outcome; after: passed
data.question: Why does ddflow ci run not record the ci gate?

evidence.note: ddflow brief read; no rule conflicts; layering/deferred-import ratchets respected (new api/cirun.py)
api/cirun.py records ci gate; full suite 12138 passed

chunk_findings.detail: The suppression flag is tested for mere presence, but the comment on `IN_GATE_ENV` says it is "Set by `gate run` in the environment of the command it runs: the gate that will record the outcome itself". The value is the *name of the running gate*, and only a `gate run <id> ci` invocation will record the `ci` gate itself. As written, any enclosing gate suppresses recording. Concrete failure: run the regression test through the project's own `unit_tests` gate, i.e. `ddflow gate run <id> unit_tests` with a test that spawns `ddflow ci run <item>` and asserts the `ci` gate got recorded. The child inherits `DDFLOW_RUNNING_GATE=unit_tests`, so `_item_here` still resolves the item but `if item and not command and not os.environ.get(IN_GATE_ENV)` is false, `_record_gate` is skipped, nothing else records `ci`, and the gate still shows the old verdict — exactly the Bec9936dc6b symptom the change is supposed to fix. The check should be scoped to the gate that owns the recording, e.g. `os.environ.get(IN_GATE_ENV) == "ci"`, not truthiness.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/cirun.py:run (the `os.environ.get(IN_GATE_ENV)` check)

chunk_findings.detail: `_item_here` claims an item whenever the caller stands in a live item's worktree, and it explicitly exempts the literal values `""`/`"HEAD"` from the "this tree's own commit" check (the comment notes "the CLI passes HEAD's sha" precisely because a literal `HEAD` is not this tree's HEAD). The tool path never performs that resolution: `ci_tool(action="run")` forwards `ref=ref or "HEAD"` unchanged to `run`, which forwards it to `CI.run(repo, cfg, ref="HEAD", ...)`. `CI.run`'s first argument is the main `repo`, so `HEAD` resolves there, not in the caller's worktree. Concrete failure: an agent standing in item W's worktree (whose branch carries the fix commit, while the main repo HEAD is behind) calls `ddflow_ci` with `action="run"` and no `ref`; `_item_here` returns W and the code records W's `ci` gate, but the CI run and `res.sha` are those of the main repo HEAD, so W's gate is recorded against a commit that was never tested for W (typically a false pass on an untested/older tree). The CLI path avoids this because it passes the caller's HEAD sha; the tool path needs the same resolution (or should not claim the item when `ref` is a bare `HEAD`).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/cirun.py:ci_tool / run (default `ref="HEAD"` vs `_item_here`)

chunk_findings.detail: The two new positive tests call `A.run(...)` (i.e. `ddflow.api.cirun.run`) in-process and assert that a record was produced (`assert res.exit == 0 and res.data["recorded"]["ok"]`, and `res.data["recorded"]["item"] == "T1"`), but they never clear `DDFLOW_RUNNING_GATE`. The same change makes `runner.py` export that variable to the gate command's environment (`"DDFLOW_RUNNING_GATE": gdef.id`), and `ci.py`/the test's own `test_a_nested_ci_run_inside_the_ci_gate_does_not_record_twice` demonstrate that cirun suppresses recording whenever that variable carries the gate id (`monkeypatch.setenv(A.IN_GATE_ENV, "ci")` ⇒ `"recorded" not in res.data`). So run the suite the way this project runs it — as a gate command, e.g. the ci gate whose `[ci] command` is the test suite, or `ddflow gate run <id> unit_tests` if cirun's check is presence-based — and pytest inherits `DDFLOW_RUNNING_GATE=ci`/`=<gate>`; `cirun.run` then takes the "leave recording to us" branch, `res.data` has no `"recorded"` key, and these two tests fail with KeyError. I.e. the regression test for "the ci gate pass is recorded" fails exactly inside the gate whose recording it is supposed to prove, turning the ci gate red again. The tests need to control that variable explicitly (`monkeypatch.delenv(A.IN_GATE_ENV, raising=False)` in the positive cases) rather than relying on it being absent from the ambient environment that `runner.py` now populates.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_gate.py:258 (test_ci_run_records_the_ci_gate_with_the_commit_it_ran_against; also the test at :~300)
